Alright, the user wants a full browser‑based CAD editor. I've already scaffolded the basic HTML (index.html) and CSS (style.css) with a top bar, canvas, and some UI elements. The next logical step is to provide the core JavaScript that powers the editor: handling document state, geometry, rendering, interaction, snapping, undo/redo, layers, properties panel, file import/export, etc.

I need to make sure the script ties into the existing DOM elements referenced in index.html (e.g., canvas, buttons with IDs like btnNew, btnOpen, btnSave, btnSvg, btnDxf, hint, coords, layerList, props, fileInput, etc.). The script should be self‑contained so that the user can just open index.html and have a functional CAD tool.

Given the complexity, I’ll write a single `app.js` file that:
1. Declares a strict mode header.
2. Sets up the document model (`doc`) with layers, activeLayer, and an entity list, plus a unique ID generator.
3. Initializes undo/redo stacks with a max depth.
4. Manages view state (pan, zoom) and canvas size variables.
5. Tracks interaction state: current tool, points collected for the active tool, cursor world position, snapping results, flags for grid/object snap, selection set, drag operation details, and modifier keys.
6. Provides DOM shortcuts (`canvas`, `ctx`, `$`) and coordinate conversion helpers (`w2sX/Y`, `s2wX/Y`, `w2s`).
7. Implements geometry helpers: distance, point‑to‑segment, angle normalization, arc sweep calculations, circumcircle for three‑point arcs, etc.
8. Defines entity model utilities: color resolution, layer visibility, segment extraction for rect/polyline, dimension geometry, text bounding box, generic bounding box per entity type, hit testing, snap point generation, and translation of entities.
9. Sets up undo/persistence functions: snapshot, mutate (push undo, clear redo, execute change), undo, redo, afterChange (save to localStorage, refresh UI, re‑render), and loadLocal (restore from storage).
10. Implements snapping: grid step calculation (nice numbers), computeSnap (object snap first, then grid), and snappedCursor (apply ortho lock when Shift is held).
11. Handles rendering: resize (handle high‑DPI), drawGrid (minor/major lines, axes), pathEntity (convert entity to canvas path), drawArrow (dimension arrows), drawDim (render dimension entities with extension lines, arrows, measurement text), drawEntity (generic entity drawing, text handling), drawSnapMarker, drawPreview (live preview for the active tool), drawSelectionGrips, render (clear, draw grid, draw all entities, draw selected entities on top, draw rubber‑band selection, preview, snap marker, crosshair).
12. Provides a formatting helper `fmt` that respects the current grid step.
13. Implements tool management: setTool, hint messages, dimFromPoints (create dimension entity from three points), addEntity (assign ID, layer, color, push via mutate), toolClick (logic for each drawing tool, handling point collection, entity creation, UI hints), finishPolyline, cancelTool.
14. Sets up mouse event handling: mousedown (pan, select, or delegate to toolClick), mousemove (update cursor, pan view, compute snap, move selected entities, update rubber‑band, update coordinate display, re‑render), mouseup (finalize pan, move, rubber‑band selection, apply copy on move if Ctrl held), dblclick (finish polyline), wheel (zoom at mouse), contextmenu (prevent default), and helper `zoomAt`.
15. Keyboard handling: space for panning, Shift for ortho, Ctrl/Meta shortcuts (undo/redo/save/select all), tool shortcuts (S, L, P, R, C, A, D, T, F, G, O, ?), Escape to cancel, Enter to finish polyline, Delete/Backspace to delete selection.
16. Snap toggles: toggleSnap for grid and object snap, updating UI button states.
17. View commands: zoomFit to fit all entities, handling empty doc case.
18. Layer UI: refreshLayers (rebuild layer list with visibility toggle, color picker, rename, delete), add layer button handler.
19. Properties UI: refreshProps (show properties for selected entities, allow editing layer, color, radius, length, text, size), helper functions addPropRow, addNumProp.
20. File operations: download helper, saveJSON (export drawing.json), open handler (file input, JSON parse, validation, replace doc, update nextId, clear selection, zoomFit), new drawing button, save button, undo/redo buttons, fit button, help toggle, snap toggle buttons, tool button click handlers.
21. SVG export: exportSVG (compute bounding box, generate SVG elements for each entity, handle arcs, polylines, text, dimensions, apply proper y‑flip, include viewBox, stroke width scaling, download as .svg).
22. DXF export (R12): exportDXF (generate DXF sections, map each entity to appropriate DXF codes, handle arcs with angle conversion, polyline, text, dimensions as geometry, download as .dxf).
23. Finally, initialization: attach resize listener, loadLocal (restore from localStorage), set initial view scale and origin, refresh UI panels, fit view if there are entities, otherwise just render.

All these pieces must be placed in the correct order so that functions are defined before they’re used where necessary, but JavaScript’s function hoisting lets me define them in a logical grouping.

I also need to ensure that any referenced DOM IDs (`canvas`, `hint`, `coords`, `layerList`, `props`, `fileInput`, `btnAddLayer`, etc.) exist in the HTML I already wrote. The CSS already defines styles for the UI elements, so the script can rely on those classes (`tool`, `active`, etc.).

Given the extensive functionality, the content will be fairly long. I’ll embed it as a string literal for the `Write` tool, targeting the file path `D:\physics\cad\app.js`. The content will start with `"use strict";` and then include all the code described above, exactly as I have drafted it.

Now I’m ready to issue the write command with the full JavaScript source.
